howItWorks.title: How the MSME {{maxDays}}-day payment rule works
howItWorks.intro: This is the law behind the calculator, in plain words. It is general information, not legal advice.

who.heading: Who is protected
who.p1: The rules protect micro and small businesses that are registered on Udyam. Your category is printed on your Udyam certificate.
who.tableCaption: Business size limits from {{date}}. A business must be within both limits for its category.
who.colInvestment: Investment in plant, machinery or equipment, up to
who.medium_note: Medium businesses are not covered by the payment deadline and interest rules. This calculator can still help you send a polite reminder.
who.trader: Traders who only buy and resell goods are generally not covered. Check with your CA.
who.registration: Your Udyam registration should exist before you supply the goods or services. Courts have linked the protection to being registered when the contract was made. Check with your CA.

deadline.heading: When the buyer must pay
deadline.p1: The clock starts on the day you deliver the goods or finish the service.
deadline.noAgreement: No written agreement: the buyer must pay within {{noAgreementDays}} days.
deadline.agreement: Written agreement: the buyer must pay within the agreed days, but never more than {{maxDays}} days. If the agreement says more, the law still uses {{maxDays}}.
deadline.objection: If the buyer objects in writing within {{objectionDays}} days of delivery, the clock starts on the day the objection is sorted out.
deadline.example: Example: you deliver on {{acceptance}} and the agreement says {{maxDays}} days. Payment is due by {{due}}. Interest starts on {{interestStart}}.
deadline.counting: We add the number of days to the delivery date. Check the exact day counting with your CA.

interest.heading: Interest on late payment
interest.p1: If the buyer pays late, they owe interest at {{multiplier}} times the RBI bank rate. Today that is {{annual}} a year ({{multiplier}} × {{bank}}).
interest.rbi: The RBI bank rate is set by the Reserve Bank of India and changes from time to time.
interest.compound: The interest is compound: at the end of each month it is added to the amount owed, and the next month’s interest is charged on the new total.
interest.daily: We use the bank rate in force on each day, so the rate can change during a long delay.
interest.noContract: No contract can reduce this interest.
interest.notDeductible: The buyer can’t claim this interest as a business expense for income tax ({{section}}).

tax.heading: The buyer’s income tax
tax.p1: A buyer normally claims payments to suppliers as a business expense, which lowers their income tax.
tax.p2: If they pay a micro or small supplier late, and the amount is still unpaid on 31 March, they can’t claim it in that tax year. They can claim it only in the year they actually pay.
tax.p3: So paying you late makes them pay more tax this year. They get the deduction later, in the year they pay.
tax.lawHeading: Which law applies depends on the tax year:
tax.estimate: To estimate the extra tax, we multiply the invoice amount by the buyer’s tax rate: {{company}} for most companies, and {{firm}} for firms and LLPs with higher income. If you don’t know the buyer’s type, we show both.
tax.estimateNote: These are estimates. The buyer’s real tax depends on their own accounts.

complaint.heading: If the buyer still doesn’t pay
complaint.p1: You can file a delayed-payment case on the {{portal}}. Since {{since}}, it is the only way to start a new case.
complaint.p2: The older MSME Samadhaan portal now handles only cases that were already filed there.
complaint.p3: The case goes to a Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: The short version: what you type stays on your device. We have no server that receives it, and we don’t use cookies.

sections.heading: Your invoice details stay on your device
sections.body: All calculations and the PDF letter are made inside your browser. Your invoice amount, dates, business details and buyer details are never sent to us or to anyone else.

sections.heading: No account, no cookies
sections.body: There is no login and no sign-up. We don’t set cookies.

sections.heading: “Remember my business details”
sections.body: Only if you tick this box, your own business details are saved in your browser’s storage on this device. Buyer and invoice details are never saved. Untick the box to delete them, or clear this site’s data in your browser.

sections.heading: WhatsApp and copied text
sections.body: When you press “Share on WhatsApp”, WhatsApp opens with a message you can edit. Nothing is sent unless you send it yourself, and WhatsApp’s own privacy terms apply. Text you copy is only on your device.

sections.heading: Visitor counts
sections.body: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics to count visits. It doesn’t use cookies and doesn’t follow you across other websites. We also count a few button presses, such as “letter downloaded”. We never record what you type into the form.

sections.heading: The early-access list
sections.body: Joining is optional. The link opens a Google Form. What you enter there goes to Google Forms and to us, under Google’s privacy policy, and is used only to tell you about new features.

sections.heading: Hosting
sections.body: The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages. Like any web host, Cloudflare handles basic technical data, such as your IP address, to deliver the pages to you.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: If anything here changes, we will update this page first.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Questions about your privacy, or a request about the early-access list? Email {{email}}.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Please read these before you rely on the calculator or send a letter.

sections.heading: Information only
sections.body: Bakaya gives general information. Nothing on this site is legal or tax advice, and using it doesn’t make us your adviser.

sections.heading: Check before you act
sections.body: Laws, RBI rates and tax rates change. We review them regularly, but we can’t promise every figure is correct or up to date for your case. Confirm amounts with your Chartered Accountant or lawyer before you send a notice or file a case.

sections.heading: Your letters
sections.body: You decide whether to send a letter and what it says. Check every detail before you send it.

sections.heading: Free, as it is
